# Project Rudis / Rudis Authority Layer
## Strategic R&D and Financing Proposal for Meta

**Prepared for:** Meta — Meta Superintelligence Labs / Meta AI / Reality Labs / Strategic Partnerships  
**Prepared by:** José Ángel Moreno Cabezas — Founder / Strategos Fundacional, Project Rudis  
**Status:** Non-binding strategic proposal for discussion and diligence  
**Current Rudis maturity:** PRE-D3 active; D3 not open; production not authorized

---

# Executive Summary

Project Rudis proposes a staged strategic R&D partnership with Meta to evaluate and integrate the **Rudis Authority Layer (RAL)**: a model-agnostic authority and execution layer designed for AI systems that can increasingly plan, delegate, call tools and act on behalf of people.

The thesis is simple:

> **Capability is not authority.**

An AI system may be able to act without therefore possessing the legitimate authority to create a real-world effect.

RAL separates:

```text
INTENT
-> IDENTITY / CLAIM
-> COMPETENCE / AUTHORITY
-> RULE EVALUATION
-> MANDATE
-> EXECUTION
-> RECEIPT
-> CONTINUITY
-> AUDIT
```

The commercial proposition is not that Rudis is already production-ready. It is that Rudis has progressed far enough to justify a serious technical partnership in which Meta can help determine whether this architecture survives realistic integration, reproduction and adversarial testing.

We propose an **initial staged program of up to USD 12 million over approximately 18 months**, with an optional subsequent program of up to **USD 15 million** only if technical, security, legal and commercial gates are satisfied.

The structure is designed to give Meta meaningful technical access, evaluation rights, reference-integration value and a preferential commercial negotiation position while preserving Project Rudis' independence and the founder's ability to continue building.

The governing commercial principle is:

```text
FAIR ECONOMIC RIGHTS FOR META
!=
TRANSFER OF RUDIS GOVERNANCE
```

---

# 1. Why this problem matters to Meta

Meta is moving from AI systems that primarily generate or recommend toward systems that can increasingly plan, connect to applications and take action on behalf of users.

That transition creates a distinct systems problem.

A model can be correct about what should happen and still lack authority to make it happen.

A session can be authenticated and still lack competence for a particular action.

A tool can be available without being legitimately invocable.

A stale authorization can remain technically well-formed after it has ceased to be valid.

A client, avatar, process or wearable can represent an actor without becoming the source of the actor's authority.

Rudis is built around preventing those category collapses.

The architecture therefore treats the following as different objects:

```text
IDENTITY != COMPETENCE
AUTHENTICATION != AUTHORITY
TOOL ACCESS != AUTHORIZATION
MODEL OUTPUT != MANDATE
SESSION != AUTHORITY
REPRESENTATION != AUTHORITY
RECOVERY != CREATION OF NEW AUTHORITY
```

For Meta, this may be relevant to:

- action-capable Meta AI;
- agent-to-application execution;
- private-preview model/API partnerships;
- AI glasses and wearable clients;
- immersive / multi-agent environments;
- internal high-value agent workflows;
- reproducible evidence for safety and security review.

The PRE-D3 campaign deliberately distinguishes:

```text
BUILDER PASS
!=
INDEPENDENT ACCREDITATION
```

and:

```text
TECHNICAL READINESS
!=
POLITICAL AUTHORIZATION
```

This discipline is part of the asset Meta would be evaluating.

# 3. The proposed Meta program

## Phase I — Diligence, convergence and independent validation

**Indicative funding: USD 1.5M**  
**Indicative duration: 90 days**

Purpose:

- establish the contracting / IP / licensing baseline;
- freeze one exact PRE-D3 evaluation candidate;
- complete a partner-readable technical architecture package;
- reproduce the candidate independently;
- perform security and adversarial review;
- define a Meta-specific threat model and integration surface;
- identify what Meta should test, reject or continue.

Indicative outputs:

- IP / license / provenance register;
- reproducible candidate package;
- independent findings register;
- security posture and residual-risk dossier;
- Meta reference-integration design;
- Phase-II go / no-go package.

Meta may stop after Phase I.

---

## Phase II — Controlled D3 laboratory

**Indicative funding: USD 4.5M**  
**Indicative duration: approximately 6 months**

Phase II begins only if the relevant technical gates are satisfied and D3 is separately authorized inside Rudis.

Purpose:

Operate an integrated candidate in a realistic but controlled environment using synthetic / internal users and controlled infrastructure.

Focus areas:

- multiple clients;
- stale authority;
- revocation;
- replay / idempotency;
- reconnect;
- session substitution;
- concurrency;
- restart and recovery;
- provider loss;
- deterministic receipts;
- causal trace reconstruction;
- artifact identity;
- client / UI inability to fabricate authority;
- independent attack.

No automatic production deployment follows from success.

---

## Phase III — Meta reference integration

**Indicative funding: USD 6M**  
**Indicative duration: approximately 9 months**

Subject to Phase-II results, Meta and Rudis select one or more high-value reference surfaces.

Potential tracks:

### A. Meta AI action gateway

```text
META AI / AGENT
-> RAL
-> AUTHORITY / RULE RESOLUTION
-> MANDATE
-> EXECUTION
-> RECEIPT
```

### B. Wearables reference client

A Meta AI glasses experience acts as an intent-producing client while authority remains external to the client.

### C. Reality Labs / Unreal reference environment

Separate avatar, session, identity, competence and authority in a persistent multi-actor environment.

### D. Internal agent operations

Apply RAL concepts to selected high-value internal agent workflows requiring stronger causal authorization and evidence.

### E. Open reference architecture

Jointly determine whether selected non-sensitive patterns should become a broader reference architecture for trustworthy agent execution.

# 6. Founder Strategic Reserve

Each funded tranche should include a clearly disclosed **Founder Strategic Reserve**.

Preferred negotiation position:

**not less than 10% of each funded tranche**, unless otherwise agreed for a particular tranche.

The founder may allocate this reserve without transaction-by-transaction Meta approval to lawful activities reasonably connected to Rudis / Quebranto, including:

- research;
- technical opportunities;
- specialist hiring;
- tooling;
- infrastructure;
- advisory work;
- travel required by the program;
- contingency;
- ecosystem development;
- strategic experiments;
- unforeseen opportunities.

The reserve remains subject to normal accounting, tax and anti-fraud obligations and can be reported in aggregate categories.

The purpose is operational speed and founder agency, not hidden spending.

```text
DISCRETION
!=
ABSENCE OF ACCOUNTABILITY
```

---

# 7. Founder compensation / liquidity

Founder personal autonomy should not depend on treating project operating funds as personal money.

The parties should therefore negotiate a **separate, transparent Founder Compensation / Liquidity Component**, structured according to legal and tax advice.

Possible forms may include:

- salary / management compensation;
- signing or transaction consideration where appropriate;
- founder bonus linked to financing or milestones;
- reimbursement of valid historical project expenditures;
- IP-license consideration where the rights and valuation justify it;
- a limited secondary transaction in a future operating company;
- another lawful mechanism agreed by the parties.

Once lawfully paid and properly taxed/accounted for, such funds are personal founder funds rather than project operating funds.

This protects both Meta and the founder by keeping personal liquidity explicit rather than obscured inside project expenditure.

---

# 8. What Meta receives

Subject to definitive agreements and diligence, Meta may receive:

- internal evaluation rights;
- controlled access to selected confidential technical materials;
- independent reproduction rights for the agreed candidate;
- security / adversarial review access;
- a dedicated Meta reference-integration track;
- technical collaboration with the Rudis architecture / engineering effort;
- milestone and financial reporting on the funded program;
- agreed audit rights over program expenditures;
- a time-limited preferred negotiation position for agreed commercial opportunities;
- an option to negotiate commercial rights to private / licensable components;
- an option to negotiate strategic investment in a future commercial vehicle.

A time-limited **Right of First Negotiation** for a narrowly defined commercial field is preferable to broad perpetual exclusivity.

---

# 9. What financing does not automatically grant

The proposal deliberately separates commercial rights from governance.

Funding alone does not grant Meta:

- ownership of the Rudis Canon;
- constitutional or legislative authority inside Rudis;
- control of Rudis institutional decisions;
- automatic control of future founder projects;
- blanket assignment of all present or future founder IP;
- perpetual worldwide exclusivity;
- unrestricted access to every private repository or vulnerability record;
- automatic ownership of all future improvements;
- rights over RU, reserves or monetary policy;
- production authorization;
- automatic expansion from D3 to D4;
- broad personal non-compete restrictions;
- personal guarantees by default.

If Meta invests in a future operating company, ordinary corporate rights can be negotiated for that company.

```text
COMPANY GOVERNANCE RIGHTS
!=
RUDIS CONSTITUTIONAL AUTHORITY
```

---

# 10. IP and licensing

Current high-level public position:

- public software is generally AGPL-3.0 unless otherwise specified;
- Corpus / documentation has a separate rights regime;
- private implementation is not publicly licensed by mere existence;
- contributor and third-party rights must be verified before commercial rights are promised;
- services, integration, hosting, support, certification, private components and official commercial relationships can be structured separately where rights permit.

Preferred transaction principles:

```text
FOUNDER / PROJECT BACKGROUND IP
-> RETAINED UNLESS EXPRESSLY LICENSED OR ASSIGNED

META BACKGROUND IP
-> RETAINED BY META

FOREGROUND IP
-> ALLOCATED BY DEFINITIVE AGREEMENT
```

No party should receive rights broader than the rights the other party actually holds.

Technical diligence will use progressive disclosure.

### Initial discussion

- public GitHub;
- public one-pager;
- RAL architecture;
- maturity statement;
- sanitized security posture.

### NDA review

- deeper architecture;
- selected evidence;

### Restricted technical review

Only where needed:

An NDA does not automatically produce unrestricted private-repository access.

# 12. Why the structure should be attractive to Meta

The proposal gives Meta substantial optionality.

Meta is not being asked to:

- acquire Rudis immediately;
- accept a speculative valuation before diligence;
- deploy an immature system;
- commit the full optional program from day one;
- trust the builder's own claims.

Instead Meta can buy information progressively.

**USD 1.5M** determines whether the technical and IP thesis merits deeper work.

**USD 4.5M** tests whether the integrated system survives realistic controlled operation and attack.

**USD 6M** is spent on a Meta-specific integration only after the earlier evidence justifies it.

The optional later program is negotiated only if there is demonstrated value.

This gives Meta asymmetric upside while limiting early commitment.

---

# 13. Success metrics

The program should be evaluated by properties rather than feature count.

### Authority integrity

No tested sensitive effect occurs without the expected authority chain.

### Currentness

Stale, revoked or indeterminate authority fails closed at the relevant boundary.

### Causal evidence

A sensitive effect can be reconstructed from claimant through rule/mandate to execution and durable state.

### Reproducibility

A party other than the builder can identify, build, run and test the agreed candidate.

### Recovery

Restart / retry / replay / reconnect do not silently create new authority or duplicate effects.

### Client separation

Agent, UI, wearable, Unreal client, session or process cannot fabricate competence merely by constructing the correct-shaped request.

### Adversarial value

Independent reviewers can reproduce failures as well as passes.

# 15. Governance and founder continuity

Meta should receive a fair economic bargain and strong contractual protection.

At the same time, Rudis should retain the ability to continue evolving independently.

Preferred founder protections include:

- ordinary-course management freedom;
- no transaction-level approval for routine engineering and operations;
- narrow reserved matters only;
- retained rights to unrelated future projects and research;
- no blanket future-IP assignment;
- no perpetual exclusivity;
- no personal guarantee by default;
- exclusivity, if any, limited by field and time and separately compensated;
- preferential rights narrowing or terminating if committed funding ceases.

This is not intended to deprive Meta of remedies for breach or misuse of funds.

It is intended to avoid converting a strategic partnership into personal or constitutional capture.

# Closing

Meta does not need to believe Rudis is correct.

The proposed partnership exists to determine whether it is.

As AI systems become more capable of acting, the distinction between what an agent **can do** and what it is **authorized to do** becomes a fundamental infrastructure problem.

Rudis is an attempt to make that distinction executable, inspectable and recoverable.

The financing structure follows the same principle as the technology:

> **Authority should be explicit, bounded and attributable.**

Meta should receive clear economic and technical rights in exchange for its capital.

The founder should retain enough independence to keep building, researching and challenging the architecture rather than becoming permanently constrained by the financing instrument itself.

```text
CAPITAL
-> CAPABILITY

CAPITAL
!=
CAPTURE
```
